scenes.text: Before any American astronaut orbited Earth, a chimpanzee named Enos did it first.
He launched from Cape Canaveral on November twenty-ninth, nineteen sixty-one.
Enos was about five years old and weighed just under forty pounds.
He had trained for over twelve hundred and fifty hours.
Only two humans had orbited Earth before him, both Soviet cosmonauts.
His job in space was to pull levers in response to flashing lights.
But a fault meant one lever gave him a small electric shock, even when he got it right.
Enos kept doing the task correctly anyway, exactly as he was trained.
Meanwhile, a stuck thruster and an overheating cabin cut the mission short.
So instead of three orbits, he came home after two, after about three hours.
He splashed down in the Atlantic, south of Bermuda.
Less than three months later, John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth.
Did you know a chimp beat every American astronaut to orbit? Tell me below.

title: The chimp who orbited Earth before any American 🐒
caption: On Nov 29, 1961, Enos the chimpanzee orbited Earth twice, 3 months before John Glenn. A faulty lever shocked him even for right answers, and he kept working anyway.
